title: Football Victoria publishes WWC Connect how-to guide for clubs
body: Football Victoria has a Working With Children Reform section on its child safety page, including a step-by-step 'How to use WWC Connect Guide' for club administrators and a link to the government webinar on the changes. The page states that all clubs must verify workers or volunteers in child related roles hold a valid Working with Children Check clearance via the WWC checker, and that clubs must also register their organisation through Services Victoria WWC Connect.
verifiedQuote: Football Victoria has developed a ' How to use WWC Connect Guide ' to assist club administrators with a step-by-step process. All clubs (organisations) must verify a worker or volunteer involved in child related roles via the WWC checker. Clubs must also register their organisation through Services Victoria WWC Connect.
correction: The source does not state that Football Victoria 'has added' a Working With Children Reform section (no timing is given), and does not use the phrase 'must register' but rather 'Clubs must also register' which appears in context of linking to the registration portal.

title: Child safety workshops for Illawarra sporting clubs, 10 to 12 November
body: The NSW Office of Sport and Wollongong City Council are running interactive child safety workshops in Wollongong, Dapto and Woonona from 10 to 12 November 2026. Delivered by the Office of Sport and the Office of the Children's Guardian, they cover de-escalating challenging behaviour, managing child safety risks and implementing Child Safe Standards. Illawarra sporting organisations can register through the Illawarra Sport Integrity Roadshow page.
verifiedQuote: The NSW Office of Sport and Wollongong City Council will host a series of interactive child safety workshops in the Illawarra next week to help local sporting organisations keep children safe from harm and abuse in sport.
correction: The workshops are not free according to the source text, which does not mention cost at all, so this claim must be removed.

title: SAFE NT closed over Christmas and New Year
body: SAFE NT, which handles Working with Children Clearances (Ochre Cards), will close its Customer Service Centre at 71 Smith St and its Call Centre from Monday 21 December 2026 to Friday 1 January 2027, reopening Monday 4 January 2027. Online self-service options stay available during the break. Clubs should remind coaches and volunteers who need in-person or phone help with an Ochre Card to contact SAFE NT before 21 December.
source: NT Police, Fire and Emergency Services (SAFE NT)
verifiedQuote: SAFE NT is taking a short end of year break, from Monday 21 December 2026 through to Friday 1 January 2027. This will include our Customer Service Centre at 71 Smith St and the Call Centre. Both will remain closed for this two-week period. We look forward to serving you in the new year, from Monday 4 January 2027. Online self-service options will continue to be available throughout the holiday period.

title: Blue Card Services webinars for clubs with volunteers
body: Blue Card Services is running online sessions on Microsoft Teams for organisations that have volunteers working with children, on 18 November and 9 December 2026. Sessions cover who needs a blue card, how to apply for a volunteer blue card and what volunteers and organisations must do under blue card laws. A Ready, Set, Compliant session on 1 December 2026 covers linking requirements, the employee register and the Organisation Portal.
verifiedQuote: Blue cards for volunteers 18 November 2026... Blue cards for volunteers 09 December 2026... Ready, Set, Compliant! 01 December 2026... linking requirements the employee register how the Organisation Portal helps you meet your legal responsibilities.
correction: The source text does not describe these as 'free' webinars, and the Ready, Set, Compliant session is on 1 December (not 'also' on that date, it's a separate session type).
